categories.criteria: Implements formal game theory concepts such as Nash bargaining, Pareto optimality, equilibrium logic, and mathematically defensible utility structures.
Accurately translates concepts from 'Multi-Task Learning as a Bargaining Game' into a new application domain while demonstrating deep understanding.
Quality of system architecture including player definitions, disagreement points, feasible allocation constraints, and implementation coherence.
Effectively compares Nash bargaining against baselines such as equal allocation, greedy allocation, and heuristic approaches while measuring fairness and efficiency.
Ability to clearly explain assumptions, defend methodology, justify choices, and present the work professionally.

grade_ranges.interpretation: Excellent formal game theory implementation, highly rigorous, publication-quality project.
Strong cooperative game theory application with minor theoretical or implementation weaknesses.
Moderately game theoretic, conceptually solid but still partially heuristic.
Paper-inspired but mathematically weak or underdeveloped.
Superficial use of terminology with poor theoretical legitimacy.
